answer_text:
We want the residue of

\[
f(z)=\frac{e^{2z}}{e^{iz}+1}
\]

at \(z=\pi\).

First check the singularity. Let

\[
g(z)=e^{iz}+1.
\]

Then

\[
g(\pi)=e^{i\pi}+1=-1+1=0.
\]

Also,

\[
g'(z)=ie^{iz},
\]

so

\[
g'(\pi)=ie^{i\pi}=-i\neq 0.
\]

Therefore \(z=\pi\) is a simple pole of \(f(z)\).

For a simple pole of \(\frac{h(z)}{g(z)}\), the residue is

\[
\frac{h(\pi)}{g'(\pi)}.
\]

Here \(h(z)=e^{2z}\), so

\[
\operatorname{Res}_{z=\pi} f(z)
=
\frac{e^{2\pi}}{-i}
=
i e^{2\pi}.
\]

Thus the residue is

\[
\boxed{i e^{2\pi}}.
\]
